name: A message waiting for approval can outlive the reason we prepared it
description:
When a round decides something about a finding from an earlier round, it prepares the message to the partner and leaves it for a reviewer to approve. Between preparing and approving, the thing that message says can stop being true — and nothing takes it back.

It showed up four separate times while building CZ3TDR1-664, and it is one question asked from four sides:

- a later round finds the problem again, so the waiting message "this looks fixed, we are closing it" is no longer what we think,
- the code moves a second time, so the waiting message still names the place the problem has left,
- the reviewer decides the finding was wrong and drops it, so a waiting reply or reopen is about a remark we no longer make,
- the reviewer changes their mind back, so a waiting "we are taking this back" is about a remark we do still make.

**Where we got to for now.** Three of those four are marked in the triage panel, so the reviewer sees a warning and cancels the message themselves. The fourth — the second move — is not marked at all, and its message keeps pointing at the old place. That asymmetry is not a decision, it is where the work stopped.

**The question this ticket is for: does the tool tidy these up, or does the person?** Marking them and leaving the click to a reviewer is what we have, and it has a real argument behind it — cancelling on its own reaches into a row somebody may be reading at that moment, and the most confrontational things this feature does should not become automatic. Tidying up on its own is more robust, because a warning informs while a cancellation removes.

**It should be answered once, for all four.** Answering it path by path is how four situations turn into three different behaviours, which is the shape of the problem rather than a fix for it. The code is already arranged so the choice is a matter of configuration rather than new logic, whichever way it goes.

**Done when:** all four behave the same way, that way is written down with its reasoning, and the fourth case stops being an omission.

Note on reach: today none of this can reach a partner, because the switch that would let the tool prepare anything at all still ships off. The exposure starts with the release.

**Sequencing note.** If this is decided after the triage panel is deployed, that is the point where a stale withdrawal can reach a partner: the panel becomes the surface where those pending messages can be approved, so an outdated one stops being a harmless record and becomes something a reviewer can send. Worth resolving before the dry-run switch is turned off.
